title: A DAY TO HUMBLE THE HEART

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "On the tenth day of this seventh month hold a sacred assembly. You must deny yourselves and do no work. Present as an aroma pleasing to the LORD a burnt offering of one young bull, one ram and seven male lambs a year old, all without defect." - Num 29:7-8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The tenth day of the seventh month was the Day of Atonement, the most solemn day in Israel's calendar. On this day the people were to "deny themselves," humbling their hearts before God, and to do no work at all. It was a day for taking sin seriously, for grieving over it, and for seeking God's cleansing with humility.

This solemn day stands in contrast to the festive gatherings around it. There is a time for joyful celebration, and there is also a time for humble self-examination before God. The Day of Atonement reminded Israel that sin is real and serious, and that reconciliation with a holy God is a weighty matter, not to be taken lightly.

We should not rush past the importance of humbling ourselves before God. In a world that avoids the discomfort of facing sin, there is deep spiritual health in taking honest stock of our hearts before the Lord. Genuine humility and grief over sin are not morbid but healing, opening the way to God's mercy.

The Day of Atonement pointed forward to the greatest act of atonement in history. On this day the high priest entered the Most Holy Place with blood; but Christ entered the true sanctuary once for all with His own blood, securing eternal redemption (Heb 9:12). The atonement Israel sought yearly, we possess forever in Him. Humble your heart before God, and rest in the perfect atonement Christ has made.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you take time to humble your heart honestly before God?
2. Why is facing our sin a path to healing rather than despair?
3. How does Christ's perfect atonement give you confidence before God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, help me to humble my heart before You and take my sin seriously. Thank You that Christ has made perfect atonement, entering the true sanctuary once for all to secure my eternal redemption. Amen.
